gilt balls above the door. <break time="0.8s" /> Holmes walked slowly up the street. <break time="0.8s" /> Then came back. <break time="0.8s" /> And thumped the pavement. <break time="0.8s" /> Two or three times with his stick. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he knocked at the shop door. <break time="0.8s" /> And a bright young man opened it. <break time="0.8s" /> And asked him to step in. <break time="0.8s" /> Holmes only asked the way. <break time="0.8s" /> To the Strand. <break time="0.8s" /> But it was the knees. <break time="0.8s" /> Of the young mans trousers. <break time="0.8s" /> That he really wanted to see. <break time="0.8s" /> He is, in my opinion. <break time="0.8s" /> The fourth smartest man in London. <break time="0.8s" /> Holmes said. <break time="0.8s" /> As we walked away from the shop. <break time="0.8s" /> We turned the corner. <break time="0.8s" /> And found a busy street. <break time="0.8s" /> Full of fine shops, offices. <break time="0.8s" /> And a branch of the City and Suburban Bank. <break time="0.8s" /> Holmes studied the buildings carefully. <break time="0.8s" /> And then spent the rest of the afternoon. <break time="0.8s" /> Listening to violin music. <break time="0.8s" /> At a concert hall. <break time="0.8s" /> That evening. <break time="0.8s" /> He told me that a serious crime was being planned. <break time="0.8s" /> And that it would take place. <break time="0.8s" /> That very night. <break time="0.8s" /> Come to Baker Street at ten. <break time="0.8s" /> He said. <break time="0.8s" /> And please bring your army revolver. <break time="0.8s" /> Because there may be some danger. <break time="0.8s" /> I went home puzzled. <break time="0.8s" /> For although I had seen and heard. <break time="0.8s" /> Everything that he had I still understood nothing.
